name: Reedgate Cut
region_detail: A shallow side channel of the lower Storbruhn near Lake Ophar.
site_type: channel | Inhabited locations | Disputed navigation channel and customary fishery.
history: Ssaresh families have maintained seasonal fish traps and reed beds along this channel for generations. River pilots recently identified it as a shortcut suitable for shallow-draft commercial vessels, and workers removed portions of the reed beds to widen the passage.
current_state: Local fishermen have driven stakes across the new boat lane, leaving a narrow opening sufficient for their own canoes. Merchant captains demand unrestricted passage, while the fishermen insist that the disturbance threatens their livelihood. Neither side has yet established exclusive control.
inhabitants: Ssaresh fishermen and their families; occasional merchant crews, independent pilots, and River Spur patrols.
danger_level: Low ordinarily; moderate if attempts to remove the obstruction provoke armed resistance.
points_of_interest:
Stake barrier; fish traps; reed beds; floating work platforms; an abandoned dredging raft; shallow alternative channels; customary fishing markers.

Unresolved elements: The extent of the channel’s customary fishing rights; Whether larger vessels can pass without damaging the fishery; Whether a compromise can preserve both navigation and local livelihoods.
discovery: A shallow side channel of the lower Storbruhn near Lake Ophar. Independent river pilots know the shortcut. Hadria Senn and Sekk Brassscale can provide accounts of its recent closure.
